Subj:  Change of duty

Ref:   (a) BUPERS msg 191325Z of January 1956

1.  Reference (a) is quoted below for your information and compliance:

     "CWO W3 DELBERT C NEWHOUSE 177283/8311 DIR DET ABT 15 FEB PROUS
     ARPROREP NATECHTRAU NAS PNCLA DUTY X DELREPARUS THIRTY DAYS X

2.  In accordance with reference (a), when directed by the Commanding Officer,
Utility Squadron FIVE, about 15 February 1956, you will regard yourself detached
from duty with Utility Squadron FIVE and from such other duty as may have been
assigned.  You will proceed to a port in the United States and upon arrival
further proceed and report to the Commanding Officer, U. S. Naval Air Technical
Training Unit, Naval Air Station, Pensacola, Florida for duty.

3.  You are hereby authorized to delay for a period of thirty (30) days, provided
no excess leave involved, in reporting in compliance with these orders, such
delay to count as leave, any portion of which may be taken prior to or after
arrival in the United States.

4.  Travel via government transportation is directed outside the United States
where available.  Class TWO priority is certified for travel via government air-
craft.  Commercial transportation authorized outside of the United States where
government transportation is not available.

5.  Cost of this travel is chargeable to appropriation 1761453.18 MPN 1956,
object class 029, expenditure account 74120, Bureau Control 22/31600.

6.  Immediately upon reporting, copies of these orders shall be forwarded to
the Chief of Naval Personnel in accordance with Art. C-5407(4), Bureau of
Naval Personnel Manual.

1.  The Selection Board, convened by the Secretary of the Navy to
recommend Naval Reserve and Temporary USN officers for appointment as
commissioned officers and warrant officers in the Regular Navy, has
considered your application for transfer, and I am pleased to inform
you that this Board has recommended you for permanent appointment in
the Regular Navy as a commissioned warrant officer.

2.  This notification is for informational purposes only, in order to
advise you of the action taken by the Selection Board on your application.
Of additional interest to you is the fact that the President has signed
Public Law #347, which provides the necessary legislation to effect the
transfer of officers to the Regular Navy.

Regular Navy will be issued to the service in a circular letter published
in the Navy Department semi-monthly bulletin.  If you are on inactive
duty you will be notified of your appointment including instructions for
acceptance.  In the event that you fail to receive this notification from
the Bureau of Naval Personnel and you find your appointment published in
the semi-monthly bulletin you may contact the nearest Naval District
Commandant for instructions and acceptance of appointment.

From:  Chief, Bureau of Aeronautics.

Subj:  LIEUTENANT DELBERT C. NEWHOUSE;  information concerning termination
       of temporary appointment.

1.  Forwarded for consideration.

2.  During the period 27 August 1948, to 29 September 1949, while on
duty at the Bureau of Aeronautics General Representative, Central Dis-
trict Headquarters, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio,
Lieutenant Newhouse served as Bureau of Aeronautics liaison officer
with the Air Materiel Command in matters relating to procurement of
photographic items under the single-service purchase assignment which
was awarded to the Air Force by the Department of Defense.

3.  On 10 August 1949, the Head of the Procurement Branch of the
Photographic Division was ordered to sea duty and it became necessary
to obtain a suitable relief.  Lieutenant Newhouse was ordered to this
duty in the Bureau of Aeronautics because of his exceptional qualifica-
tions and recent experience in procurement procedures gained while on
duty at Air Materiel Command Headquarters, Dayton, Ohio.  He is now
serving as Head of the Procurement Branch, Photographic Division, during
which time his services have been entirely satisfactory.

                         T.C. Lonnquest

Encl:  (1) Transcripts of portions of representative fitness reports

1.  I received reference (a) on 25 October 1949 notifying me that my
temporary appointment as lieutenant would terminate on 31 December 1949.

2.  Reference (b) published the policy for the priority of reversion
of temporary officers and asserted that it was highly desirable that
reductions be effected on a logical basis, considering both the best
interests of the service and the most equitable consideration of the
temporary officers concerned.  Paragraph 2(d) stated that temporary
officers, permanent commissioned warrant, would be reverted in ascending
order of retirement dates.

3.  After receipt of reference (a), I have made a careful examination
of my correspondence and fitness report files in the Bureau of Naval
Personnel.  Material of a possibly adverse nature was disclosed by
this examination in that an officer's fitness report dated 29 February
1948 was checked in the unfavorable box and was signed by Captain J.
C. Cronin, USN, then Commander Utility Wings, Pacific.  A partial
transcript thereof is appended hereto as Exhibit "A" of Enclosure (1).
This was my first report from this command and covered the period from
23 October 1947 to 29 February 1948.  I was transferred from the com-
mand on 1 July 1948 and a transcript of section 12 of my next and final
fitness report from Captain Cronin is appended hereto as Exhibit "B"
of Enclosure (1).

4.  The balance of all my fitness reports have ranged from above average
to superior and, almost without exception, have recommended retention
in temporary rank, transfer to regular commissioned rank, and promotion
when eligible.  Exhibits "C" through "G" to Enclosure (1) are submitted
as being truly representative of my fitness as an officer.

ENCLOSURE (1)

Exhibit "A"        29 February 1948        Captain J. C. Cronin, USN

12. "Unfavorable."

Lt. Newhouse is a reserved, cheerful, and generally likeable officer.
He is having a most difficult time adjusting himself to staff duty.
He is judged competent in the technical aspects of photography, but
his performance of his administrative duties in both the photographic
and operational departments is below average. It is felt that his
deficiency is principally due to his background and lack of experience
in administration. He is making a sincere effort to correct this
deficiency. He is not yet fitted for promotion.


Exhibit "B"        1 July 1948        Captain J. C. Cronin, USN

12. "Satisfactory."

Lt. Newhouse is a quiet, reserved, and likeable officer. He has had
a difficult time adjusting himself to his duties on this staff, but
he has earnestly endeavored to do so. If his experience in naval
aviation had been wider, it is believed he would have performed his
duties better. He has performed his technical duties as Photographic
Officer well. His performance of administrative duties, both as
Photographic Officer and as Assistant Operations Officer, has improved
during the period of this report. He is not yet fitted for promotion.


Exhibit "C"        19 August 1946        Admiral E. D. Foster,SC,USN

12. "Satisfactory."

Lt. Newhouse has carried out his duties as Photographic Liaison Officer
in a manner which has reflected credit on this Depot. He has a confident
and quiet manner and excellent military conduct. His screening of
photographic requests and handling of photographic problems has dis-
played an initiative and thoroughness which is most desirable for an
officer in his particular billet. Lt. Newhouse is recommended for pro-
motion when due and for commissioned rank in the regular Navy.

1.  Your application for transfer to commissioned limited duty status
has been carefully considered by the Selection Board convened by the
Secretary of the Navy.  I regret to inform you that your name was not
included among those recommended for appointment.  However, I wish to
assure you that this decision is no reflection upon your performance
of duty in the Navy; nor will it in any way affect your present status
or preclude your making application and being considered by subsequent
selection boards.

2.  The number of applicants desiring transfer to commissioned limited
duty status has been far in excess of the number of appointments which
can be offered.  Therefore, it was necessary for the Selection Board
to recommend, from among eligible applicants, only those best qualified
for appointment.  The decision in your case was made after a careful
review of your entire record and your qualifications as compared with
those of other applicants of your rank and classification or enlisted
rating.

3.  The interest you have shown in pursuing a naval career represents
an exemplary attitude of service and patriotism.  The Navy is sincerely
appreciative of your contribution toward maintaining the naval estab-
lishment at a high level of efficiency during the war, the demobiliza-
tion period, and the continuing period of world unrest.

EXPLANATION OF SCORES

1. The scores are given in percentiles. The percentile scores run from 01 to 99 and indicate the percent of candidates receiving a lower score. Thus, if a candidate has a percentile score 63, 63 percent of the candidates taking the test made a lower score and 37 percent had the same or a higher score.

2. It should be noted that the total score percentile is not an average of the percentiles for the sections, but indicates a candidate's relative standing on the basis of his total test score. Candidates with a generally high record on the test will have a percentile on the total score that is higher than the average of their percentiles on the sections. Similarly, candidates with a generally low record on the test will have a lower percentile on the total score than the average of their section percentile scores.

INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS CONCERNING THIS ELECTION FORM
(For Nonretired members)

1.    It is desired that all members with 17 years service creditable for basic pay purposes, active or inactive, either decline or elect to provide certain annuities for their dependents under the provisions of the Uniformed Services Contingency Option Act of 1953 (Public Law 239-83rd. Congress). If you desire to receive a reduction in the retired pay which you may subsequently receive, thereby providing an annuity for your dependents, you must elect the desired option(s) not later than 30 April 1954 or prior to completion of 18 years service creditable for basic pay purposes, whichever is later. The terms of the election may be modi-fied or revoked prior to retirement, but any modification or revocation will not be effective if you retire within five years from the date of such modification or revocation.

2.    If you do not desire to receive reduced retired pay to provide an annuity for your dependents, check the square opposite "I do not desire to receive reduced retired pay in order to provide an annuity for my dependents" on the face of this form, sign all copies of the form and return it to the Bureau of Naval Personnel, Washington 25, D. C.  You may subsequently elect to be covered by this Act, provided you submit such election to the Bureau of Naval Personnel, Washington 25, D. C., not later than 30 April 1954 or prior to completion of 18 years service creditable for basic pay purposes, whichever is later.

3.    If you desire to receive reduced retired pay to provide an annuity for your dependents, fill out the form completely check-ing desired option(s); all copies must be signed and notorized or attested.

4.    If either Option 2 or 3 is elected, it is required that all eligible children be named.

5.    If should be noted that, under Option 3, all benefits are paid to the widow until her death or remarriage and thereafter in equal shares to or on behalf of the surviving children remaining eligible at the time the payment is due. Consequently, if it is desired that children of a former marriage receive payments concurrently with the widow, Options 1 and 2 should be elected.

6.    In indicating the place of dissolution of a former marriage, please include the city, county and state.

7.    The triplicate of this form is to be retained by you for your personal file.  For active duty personnel, the original will be forwarded to the Bureau of Naval Personnel, Washington 25, D. INSTRUCTIONS

(Items for which no instructions are printed below are self-explanatory)

IF NECESSARY, CONTINUE ANY ITEM IN "REMARKS" BUT SPECIFY THE PARTICULAR ITEM BEING CONTINUED.

All items of this form MUST be completed and MAINTAINED CURRENT by all officers and enlisted personnel in accordance with the following: NAVY—BuPers Manual, Art. B2312; MARINE CORPS—Par. 4019, PRAM; U. S. COAST GUARD—Personnel Manual, Par. 13–B–14.

In the event you, the designator, should die, the persons or agencies named in items 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 19 will be notified unless item 15 shall indicate a person or persons NOT to be notified.

Should you become critically or seriously ill, or incapacitated to the extent that you cannot notify them, the persons named in items 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 will be notified unless item 15 shall indicate a person or persons NOT to be notified.

Payment of any benefits and disposition of remains in case of death shall be in accordance with applicable law.

Item 10.—Enter full name and address of wife or husband. For wife, use given names, for example, "Marion Elizabeth Dawson." If the designator is single, divorced, or widowed, so state.

Items 12 and 13.—The term "Father" and/or "Mother" shall be interpreted to include "natural," "step," "adoptive" and person who stood in "loco parentis" to the designator for a period of not less than 1 year at any time prior to designator's entry upon active service.

Item 14.—In the event that there is no other adult next of kin other than those named in items 10, 12 and 14, you may name a friend here. However, if a friend is named, he or she must be so identified.

Item 14a.—Enter under this item, the names of those persons who are in fact actually receiving more than 50 percent of their support from the designator. The information thus furnished shall be used in connection with other determinations of dependency under existing or future laws.

Item 16.—Enter the name, address, and relationship of beneficiary (or beneficiaries) whom you desire to receive the 6 months' death gratuity in the event you are not survived by a spouse or eligible child(ren). The succession of eligible survivor's as set forth in the "Servicemen's and Veterans" Survivor

Benefits Act," P. L. 881–84th Congress, is as follows: (1) Spouse; (2) Children (without regard to their age or marital status) in equal shares; (3) Parents or brothers or sisters (including those of halfblood and those by adoption), when so designated; (4) Parents in equal shares; or (5) Brothers and sisters (including those of halfblood or those by adoption) in equal shares.

NOTE:
The payment to either category (4) or (5) is in the event that a designation is not made under category (3).
The term "parents" includes "natural parents," "stepparents," "adoptive parents" and persons who stood in "loco parentis" to the designator for a period of not less than 1 year at any time prior to the designator's entry upon active service.

Item 17.—Enter name and address of the beneficiary or beneficiaries whom you desire to receive any unpaid pay and allowances (Arrears of Pay) due you at the time of death. There are no restrictions on who may be designated as a beneficiary or beneficiaries to receive unpaid pay and allowances and once a designation has been made it is binding until superseded by the completion of a later DD Form 93–1.

Item 18.—The "Missing Persons Act" provides that pay and allowances continue to accrue to the pay account of any service member for the period he is missing or captured and may be paid to the dependents for support. This item reflects your desires and is used as a guide in the disposition of your pay. Allotments to dependents and insurance companies initiated prior to entering a missing status are continued in effect unless unusual circumstances indicate changes.

Item 21.—The person assigned, by the commanding officer, the responsibility for interviewing the designator will, upon completion of the form, witness the designator's signature and sign in block 21.

INSTRUCTIONS

(Items for which no instructions are printed below are self-explanatory)


IF NECESSARY, CONTINUE ANY ITEM IN "REMARKS" BUT SPECIFY THE PARTICULAR ITEM BEING CONTINUED.

   All items of this form MUST be completed and MAINTAINED CURRENT by all officers and enlisted personnel in accordance with the following: NAVY–BuPers Manual, Art. B2312; MARINE CORPS–Par. 4019, PRAM; U. S. COAST GUARD– Personnel Manual, Par. 13–B–14.

   In the event you, the designator, should die, the persons or agencies named in items 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 19 will be notified unless item 15 shall indicate a person or persons NOT to be notified.

   Should you become critically or seriously ill, or incapacitated to the extent that you cannot notify them, the persons named in items 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 will be notified unless item 15 shall indicate a person or persons NOT to be notified.

   Payment of any benefits and disposition of remains in case of death shall be in accordance with applicable law.

   Item 10.–Enter full name and address of wife or husband. For wife, use given names, for example, "Marion Elizabeth Dawson." If the designator is single, divorced or widowed, so state.

   Items 12 and 13.–The term "Father" and/or "Mother" shall be interpreted to include "natural," "step," "adoptive" and person who stood in "loco parentis" to the designator for a period of not less than 1 year at any time prior to designator's entry upon active service.

   Item 14.–In the event that there is no other adult next of kin other than those named in items 10, 12 and 14, you may name a friend here. However, if a friend is named, he or she must be so identified.

   Item 14a.–Enter under this item, the names of those persons who are in fact actually receiving more than 50 percent of their support from the designator. The information thus furnished shall be used in connection with other determinations of dependency under existing or future laws.

   Item 16.–Enter the name, address, and relationship of beneficiary (or beneficiaries) whom you desire to receive the 6 months' death gratuity in the event you are not survived by a spouse or eligible child(ren). The succession of eligible survivor's as set forth in the "Servicemen's and Veterans" Survivor

Benefits Act," P. L. 881–84th Congress, is as follows: (1) Spouse; (2) Children (without regard to their age or marital status) in equal shares; (3) Parents or brothers or sisters (including those of halfblood and those by adoption), when so designated; (4) Parents in equal shares; or (5) Brothers and sisters (including those of halfblood or those by adoption) in equal shares.

NOTE:
   The payment to either category (4) or (5) is in the event that a designation is not made under category (3).
   The term "parents" includes "natural parents," "stepparents," "adoptive parents" and persons who stood in "loco parentis" to the designator for a period of not less than 1 year at any time prior to the designator's entry upon active service.

   Item 17.–Enter name and address of the beneficiary or beneficiaries whom you desire to receive any unpaid pay and allowances (Arrears of Pay) due you at the time of death. There are no restrictions on who may be designated as a beneficiary or beneficiaries to receive unpaid pay and allowances and once a designation has been made it is binding until superseded by the completion of a later DD Form 93–1.

   Item 18.–The "Missing Persons Act" provides that pay and allowances continue to accrue to the pay account of any service member for the period he is missing or captured and may be paid to the dependents for support. This item reflects your desires and is used as a guide in the disposition of your pay. Allotments to dependents and insurance companies initiated prior to entering a missing status are continued in effect unless unusual circumstances indicate changes.

   Item 21.–The person assigned, by the commanding officer, the responsibility for interviewing the designator will, upon completion of the form, witness the designator's signature and sign in block 21.

From:  Commanding Officer, USS ESSEX (CVA9)
To:    All Hands, USS ESSEX (CVA9)
       Commander, Air Task Group 201

Subj:  Commendation for Operations performed during
       Mediterranean and WesPac Deployment

1.  The Commanding Officer is in receipt of many complimentary
communications concerning the outstanding performance of ESSEX
and Air Task Group 201 during the period 2 February to
17 November 1958.

2.  During this period ESSEX and her embarked Air Group served
as a striking unit of the Sixth Fleet in Mediterranean waters,
and her aircraft provided initial and sustained air support
for U. S. Marine landings in Lebanon from 15 July to August
1958.  These operations, under wartime conditions, were per-
formed by the men of ESSEX and ATG 201 with an outstanding
degree of professional skill and devotion to duty.

3.  Following this, ESSEX was deployed on an emergency basis
to the Far East, where air operations in support of U. S.
National policy during the Formosa crisis were conducted in
the same outstanding manner.

4.  Indicative of the performance of ESSEX and her Air Group
are the following excerpts from various communications
received:

     a.  In a letter of March 28, 1958, RADM N. S. HENDERSON,
O.B.E., RN, Vice Naval Deputy, Supreme Headquarters, Allied
Powers Europe who was on board observing operations, stated....
"But above all I took away an impression of a quietly effi-
cient ship with a very lively crew, all of whom seemed keen
and interested in the job.  I was deeply impressed...."

     b.  From Commander Sixth Fleet...."AM DELIGHTED WITH A
RECENT LETTER RECEIVED FROM COMMANDING OFFICER TENCH REPORT-
ING THE OUTSTANDING TREATMENT ACCORDED TENCH AND SEA ROBIN
BY YOU WHILE IN COMPANY DURING YOUR RECENT VISIT TO PALMA X
IT IS TRULY HEART WARMING TO LEARN OF THE WHOLEHEARTED
COOPERATION AND MUTUAL SUPPORT BETWEEN UNITS OF THE SIXTHFLT X

CWO NEWHOUSE is a very competent and well informed officer whose performance as

facilities very effectively, always meeting the demands placed on his section and
working in harmony with all departments on the ship.  He is the type of officer who,

administration of section by CWO NEWHOUSE.  CWO NEWHOUSE is a very likeable and congenial
